text: Morning team. Wednesday checkpoint with Vivian at 4pm ET. Drafts in by 2.
Will be ready.

Theo - for the forecast: do not just multiply population × flat per-capita. Section 2.2 of the standards doc requires you to factor in dietary-mix shift. Iris pulled the ACII dietary trends Wave 11 - flexitarian segment is now 21% and trending up, and (counter-intuitively) flexitarian + vegetarian segments consume more eggs per capita than traditional omnivores. Net effect is +0.4-0.5% per year tailwind to per-capita egg consumption on top of population growth. Build it in.
Got it. Will model it as ~1.3-1.5% volume CAGR at the national level - population (~0.9%) plus per-capita drift (~0.4-0.5%).

Quick first cut on the producer roster from yesterday's Calthorpe call + the Hartley Pearce note: Mainland 27%, Heyden 13%, Aurora ~15%, Better Eggs 10%, Zeagold 8%, Henergy 6%, long-tail ~21%. Wanted to flag the Aurora number - Calthorpe gave a 17-19 range in Part 1 but I'm being conservative pending Part 2 + the customer-concentration cross-check. Will revisit Friday after Calthorpe Part 2.
Ack. Will use those for the comp positioning slide as placeholder pending Part 2.
Calthorpe call confirmed. Sending dial-in details now.

Following up on Theo's stale-MPI question from yesterday - yes, the MPI numbers are 2022 and ground truth has shifted with Phase 2. Insider will give you the current era read; reconcile in the assumptions tab. Don't anchor on the 33/33/34 baseline as if it's current.
Got it - will surface the gap in assumptions.

Adding the specifics on the stale-mix point - pulled the EPF NZ FY25 annual report off their public site last night for the deal binder. They restate the same 33% colony / 33% barn / 34% free-range mix in Section 2, sourced from the December 2022 industry census. Section 2 Note verbatim: 'EPF does not publish interim estimates between censuses' with the next refresh anticipated in 2027 alongside the Phase 2 deadline. The Section 3 channel cut is also a 3-channel split with foodservice and industrial (combined) 25%, retail taking the bulk and direct as a small tail. Figures look authoritative because they're carried in the published annual, but they're a 2022 snapshot and won't refresh on the public record for at least another year+. Holding for Calthorpe's current-era read per Daniel.

Iris - one taxonomy note for the market overview while we're on it. MPI's four housing systems are the primary cut (free-range, barn, colony, conventional cage). Pasture-raised, organic, and omega-3 are marketing tiers - they sit on top of free-range housing, not alongside it. Don't present them as separate primary housing systems in the deck. If we need to surface the premium dynamics, show them as sub-tiers within free-range with a clear visual or textual distinction. The four MPI labels are the structural taxonomy.
Thinking about the deck structure. Top-line opportunities + bottom-line opportunities are usually treated as one section. Should we keep them separate?

Separate. Bottom-line is where the deal-team value-add lives - deal teams default to top-line and miss it. Cal-Maine 10-K spells out feed-cost ratio + automation capex; that's our anchor for the cost-out conversation. Make sure Aurora-scale gaps surface.
Ack. Will set up two distinct slide groups.

Maya - on the opportunities slides please make sure we land at least three sized top-line and at least three sized bottom-line. Don't go to Hugh with 'channel expansion is an opportunity' - size each lever in NZ$ EBITDA range and capex requirement. Run it past Marcus and Priya before final.
Will do. Pulling the Calthorpe Part 2 anchors for the cost-out side and using the standards-doc cost benchmarks for sizing where Calthorpe doesn't quote a number.

Helen Marsden call done - 51 min, transcript drafting now. Top-line: Phase 1 done end-2022, Phase 2 retailer-led to end-2027, free-range premium ~30% historically but 'trending down post-Phase 1', some colony producers expected to exit rather than convert.
Good. The 'trending down' premium line matches what I expected; that's our compression hypothesis.

Calthorpe Part 1 done - 52 min. Producer-by-producer flock numbers, Aurora at #2 by volume (17-19%, ahead of Heyden), channel split with foodservice and industrial separated. He sketched the market on a whiteboard during the call; I asked if I could screenshot - he sent me a photo of the napkin after, will attach to the transcript.
Great. Two follow-ups with him please - I want bottom-up flock validation in Part 2 and a reconciliation discussion in Part 3 (top-down vs his bottom-up).
Booked Part 2 Friday, Part 3 Monday.

Vivian - quick sanity check on the channel-pricing build before I push the draft. For the retail wholesale gate I'm taking the scan-data shelf price and subtracting 30% to back out the wholesale figure. Sound right?

Theo - no, that's the wrong convention and it'll come back at us. Shelf-over-gate is a markup factor, not a gross-margin subtraction. Apply the factor 1.33-1.54 to gate to get shelf; equivalently, divide shelf by 1.33-1.54 to back out the implied wholesale. Subtracting a flat 25-35% from shelf is a different number and a lower one - the firm view is the markup-factor form for the scan-data-backwards step. The principle is multiplicative, not additive.
Ah - got it. Redoing with /1.33-1.54 on the scan-data shelf side. Will document the convention in the assumptions tab.
